purpose: The originality half of the IP programme had never produced a number. The screening tool was written and correct and had never run against anything - status CORPUS_REQUIRED, blocker APPROVED_OFFLINE_EXTERNAL_CORPUS_NOT_PROVIDED - so 'is the protected core original' stood unmeasured while being read as unfavourable. One corpus needs no approval and no network: the packages this repository already depends on, which is also the likeliest way third-party code reaches a first-party module by accident. 688 protected files were screened against 23 084 files from 1146 packages. 78 findings, affecting exactly 2 files, both re-export barrels with zero characters of non-re-export code. No verdict is claimed and no ASVS decision is touched.
requiredInvariants: The screening tool is not modified. Its normalisation, fingerprints, thresholds and refusals are exactly as they were; this branch supplies a corpus it can read and records what came back.

The corpus is rebuildable from the lockfile rather than shipped. Nothing under node_modules is committed, the builder hard-links from the store so the corpus costs no additional space, and the record carries the aggregate digest so a rerun can be compared against this one.

The corpus is re-rooted so no node_modules segment survives. The screening tool excludes any path containing one - correctly, or it would scan our own installed tree and call our dependencies our own code - and pnpm stores packages at .pnpm/<id>/node_modules/<name>. Pointed at the store directly the run would report a clean result over an empty corpus, which is the most dangerous possible outcome because it looks like proof. The suite asserts this invariant directly.
A clean result is not reported until the run is shown capable of a dirty one. Two files were planted in the protected core and both were caught; the planted files were removed and the tree restored.

The two findings are classified by measurement, not by reading them. Both files contain zero characters once re-export lines and comments are removed, so the match is a property of barrel files rather than a judgement about these two.

The record states its own limits in its own text: it does not address any corpus outside the dependency store, and it says nothing about authorship, which is a separate claim with separate evidence and remains blocked on four owner documents.
acceptance: 688 protected files screened against 23 084 corpus files from 1146 packages; 78 findings; exactly 2 source files affected; 0 substantive.
Both affected files measure 0 characters of non-re-export code, so the classification is mechanical.

Falsification: a verbatim copy of zod/src/v3/types.ts (5 138 lines) planted in the protected core is caught as EXACT_SHA256, and the same file with comments stripped as NORMALIZED_TOKENS - on the same corpus and settings that report the core clean.
The corpus rebuilds reproducibly: 1146 packages, 69 582 regular files, 0 non-regular entries, no additional disk used.
build-dependency-corpus.test.mjs passes 5 of 5, including that no corpus entry name can contain a node_modules segment and that a symlinked package directory is not counted as a package.
No ASVS decision, no verdict and no application code is touched; the matrix is unchanged against main.
